caption: I'm Maya. My life changes, but I keep building on one health history in Stellis.
2022: I start with tiredness, my actual period dates, and an appointment with my doctor.
I keep a confirmed appointment separate from a plan. I check the details before saving.
I bring in my original reports. They enter Maya's isolated demo workspace, using the app's record import.
I review the visit and test dates against the original documents before confirming them.
I choose the notebooks that share these records. One history can belong in more than one part of my care.
The original blood result stays available. Hemoglobin and ferritin are different findings, with their own values and dates.
I keep my own follow-up notes in the same notebook. These are my words, saved in the app.
2024–25: fertility investigations lead to treatment, pregnancy and becoming a parent. I don't start my history over.
The next source packages extend the same library. I confirm their dates and notebook filing through the same review flow.
I inspect the actual monitoring record. Dose changes retain their date and context; I don't turn them into a generic health score.
Pregnancy and postpartum records stay connected. An estimated due date remains different from the actual birth.
2026: my periods return and iron follow-up matters again. Earlier notebooks and my own notes are still here.
I enter the medicine course from its source: dose, alternate-day schedule and recorded supply. I review it before saving.
Logging is a separate decision. I review the dated entry and confirm before it becomes part of my history.
The notebook Brief brings the saved course and its calculated dates together with the original records.
For a new visit, recording and personal notes live in the same interface. This is the ready state, not a claimed transcription run.
Measurements are part of this same app. I enter dated values from my records, then inspect the chart and table directly.
Now try a fresh reading of your own. Your camera test stays separate from my sample history.
Pause here to try the live camera. Rest, face the light, and choose Start when you're ready. Video stays on your device.
This recording host has no physical camera. The real recovery state stays visible; no sample number is presented as live inference.
From a first concern to changing care and a new routine, I have grown my history. The earlier source and my notes are still part of it.
